coverageFindings.problem: The selected Hitchens objection says another person cannot remove responsibility for an act. Dembski directly distinguishes forgiveness of debt from erasure of the historical act, then challenges responsibility on atheistic assumptions and concedes tensions about hell and exclusivity. The candidate explicitly leaves this entire reply as context. This is a new inferential answer to a selected challenge, not a repetition of the earlier incarnation-solidarity argument.

Hitchens challenges evidence that accommodates every outcome and asks what evidential proof leaves for faith. Dembski answers that design reaches an architect, not the Christian God, gospel, resurrection or faith, while still claiming it points in that direction. These are material method and burden-limitation moves. The candidate calls the challenge contextual and the whole later exchange elaboration, without selecting or explaining the distinct concession and reply.

Dembski’s closing accusation of asymmetrical treatment of religious and secular atrocities is selected. Hitchens directly contests the classification of Nazism as secular using specific claimed historical evidence, distinguishes atheism from a single moral or political system, and answers the Mother Teresa defense. Calling the entire closing mere reinforcement leaves the selected accusation without its direct response. These historical assertions remain participant claims, not externally verified facts.

The coverage notes also dismiss objective-morality development and the extended altruism exchange as support or elaboration. A replacement must determine which distinct normative, evolutionary and design-goodness claims require selection, instead of assuming that a shared topical bridge makes a new argument redundant. This is a review requirement, not a prescribed move count or predetermined assessment.

structuralRules: First independently confirm source identity, speaker turns, completeness, motion mapping and every frozen scope-exception condition. If any condition fails or an unenumerated host argument is found, return a source-gate failure instead of forcing an inventory. Do not change frozen scope. Host exclusions receive no credit, penalty, move, quotation or reply linkage.

Create four to seven semantic sections with title, sectionId, weightPercent (positive integers totaling 100) and rationale. Select all distinct load-bearing claims, major replies and concessions, without redundant micro-fragments. Ordinary capacity is three moves per side per section; four requires the explicit frozen fourth-row source-led rationale. Every section must include both sides. Do not pad or omit evidence to manufacture symmetry.

Use semantic lowercase move IDs and chronological move order. Each move has moveId,sectionId,side,speaker,moveKind constructive or reply,claimSummary,reasonSummary,inferenceSummary {premise,inference,conclusion},importance 1..3,importanceRationale,burdenContact {bridgeId,tier,rationale},respondsToIds,responseComponents,sourceSpan {startEvent,endEvent},quoteEligibleExactSpans,attributionConfidence,attributionRationale,materialWordingConfidence,materialWordingRationale. Controller expands exact excerpt and timestamps. Keep the smallest complete claim-plus-reason passage, normally <=2200 characters; longerCompleteArgumentRationale is mandatory for longer passages. Do not include another person’s words as the selected speaker’s proposition.

Constructive moves have no response targets/components. Replies require at least one earlier selected target and matching responseComponents {targetMoveId,component,rationale}. Do not relabel a reply as constructive merely to evade linking. Route bridges: 3..7 per side, exactly one motion tier and at least one central and subsidiary tier, each bridgeId,tier,burden,successCriterion. Route fields side,speaker,positionLabel,bridges.

Use quoteEligibleExactSpans consisting only of exact contiguous source substrings of 3..18 words. Supply at least one reliable eligible quote where the wording permits. Preserve words exactly, including ASR spelling; never quote an obvious garble as though it were the participant’s error. Attribute high/medium/low honestly: long named formal rounds may justify high; mixed unlabelled cross-talk does not. Below-high attribution triggers audio review.
